function.mechanism: Triphosphates chelate metal ions and modify ionic balance/pH, supporting texture, water retention, and formulation stability in processed foods.

adi.basis: EFSA 2019 group ADI for phosphates (E338-341, E343, E450-452), expressed as phosphorus.

efsa.key_finding: EFSA set a group ADI of 40 mg/kg bw/day (as phosphorus); exposure exceeded ADI in several child/high-intake scenarios, and supplement exposure may exceed ADI.

adi.basis: JECFA group MTDI for phosphorus from all sources, expressed as P (latest E451(i) entry shows same MTDI).

concerns.summary: EFSA identified kidney calcification/tubular nephropathy as the critical effect for phosphate risk characterization and noted ADI non-applicability to moderate-severe renal impairment.
Recent reviews describe plausible cardiorenal pathways from high inorganic phosphate additive intake, including vascular calcification and mineral-hormone dysregulation.
A 2025 mouse study found anxiety-like behavior and neuroimmune changes under chronic high-phosphate diet conditions.

no_concern_confirmed: EFSA found no concern regarding genotoxicity and carcinogenicity for the phosphate additive group.
EFSA reported no developmental toxicity signal in the phosphate group dataset.
No IARC classification entry was identified for E451 names in the reviewed IARC classification dataset.

adi_exceedance.notes: EFSA reported ADI exceedance in analytical-data scenarios for younger groups and noted supplement-related exceedance.

risk_assessment.rationale: E451 remains authorized in major frameworks, but EFSA set a finite group ADI and identified exceedance in multiple population scenarios, especially younger/high consumers; mechanistic and emerging animal evidence supports caution at high exposure.
key_factors: EFSA group ADI 40 mg/kg bw/day (as phosphorus)
EFSA-reported ADI exceedance in infants/toddlers/children and high-consuming adolescents
FDA GRAS status for sodium tripolyphosphate (21 CFR 182.1810) under GMP
JECFA group MTDI 70 mg/kg bw/day (as P)
No IARC listing for triphosphate additive names in the reviewed classification dataset
